title: etcd-compaction-backup-interaction-retrospective-draft
content:
Summary:

Short version: On 2025-10-22 between 02:03–02:21 UTC we observed a control-plane availability incident triggered by a backup job and compact/defrag work happening concurrently on all etcd leaders. The backup orchestration ran snapshot+defrag processes in parallel across the three control-plane nodes during peak write tail (rolling model configs), which caused sustained disk IO saturation on the etcd data volume. Etcd server p99 latencies spiked from ~3ms to ~1200ms, the leader experienced election flaps, API server requests timed out, kube-scheduler fell behind and several nodes began reporting kubelet timeouts and a small eviction wave followed. Impact: short API errors for customer requests (5m error window for some critical routes), increased pod restart churn across several control-plane managed workloads, and elevated SLO error budget consumption for 1 hour.

Immediate timeline (UTC):
- 01:58: scheduled backup cron triggered as usual (daily full snapshot + defrag) across control-plane nodes (cron job in infra/backup-runner released last week).
- 02:03: first signs of elevated etcd request latency in our synthetic control-plane probe (api-health p50/p99). Pager fired for etcd high latency.
- 02:05: API server 5xxs increase; internal dashboard shows kube-apiserver request timeouts to etcd endpoints.
- 02:06: ops oncall (Maya) starts triage, confirms disk iops on control-plane nodes nearing max.
- 02:08: etcd leader election observed in logs (leader changed twice within 120s).
- 02:10: kube-scheduler backlog grows, pods entering Pending due to controller timeouts.
- 02:13: backup runner completes snapshot on node-a but immediately starts defrag+compact operation; node-b and node-c follow in quick succession.
- 02:18: we manually paused the backup-runner cron and disabled the scheduled job for the rest of the window; CPU remained normal but disk wait remained high until defrag processes finished.
- 02:21: etcd latencies returned to near-normal; control-plane stabilized by 02:30.

Root cause analysis (current draft):
- The backup-runner orchestration was configured to start snapshot+defrag jobs on all control-plane nodes within the same maintenance window without any per-node rate limiting.
- The defrag/compaction operations are IO-heavy and during high-write periods (model config rollouts and key churn) they push etcd disk queue depth above provisioned baseline, causing high wait times.
- Etcd writes block on disk fsyncs; while leader worked, follower catches-up operations increased the IO pressure further, leading to high etcd server-side RPC latencies and transient leader instability.
- Lack of guardrails: no checkpointing of write-rate vs. defrag job start, and no automatic stalling of compaction if disk iowait passes threshold.

Why this caused downstream failures:
- API server depends synchronously on etcd for many reads/writes; when etcd latency rises API server requests time out leading to 5xxs and controllers queuing operations.
- Scheduler and controller-manager observe delays in endpoints/status updates and requeue work; backlog leads to pod Pending/Restart cycles in edge cases where readiness probes or leader-election timeouts occur.

Metrics & logs (selected):
- etcd_server_apply_duration_seconds p99: baseline 0.003s -> peak 1.2s at 02:07 UTC.
- node-controlplane-disk-iowait: baseline 0.4% -> peak 82% during defrag.
- kube-apiserver 5xx rate: +210% between 02:05–02:12.
- journalctl excerpt (node-a):
  Oct 22 02:06 etcd[1234]: rafthttp: handlePeerMsg: read tcp 10.0.0.1:2380->10.0.0.2:55560: i/o timeout
  Oct 22 02:07 etcd[1234]: 2025-10-22 02:07:12.123456 W | etcdserver: read-only range request "kube/apiserver/.." timed out

Triage commands run (for reproducibility):
- etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.0.0.1:2379 endpoint status --write-out=table
- curl -sS -k https://127.0.0.1:2379/health | jq .
- kubectl get componentstatuses; kubectl get events --all-namespaces --since=15m
- sar -d 1 10 (disk metrics sampling)
- ps aux | grep etcd; lsof /var/lib/etcd/member/wal

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- Disabled scheduled backup-runner for the daily full snapshot (manual flag flip).
- Temporarily increased disk IOPS provisioning for control-plane volumes (hotfix on cloud provider) to buy headroom while defrag completed.
- Re-ordered backups to run sequentially (manual intervention) and ensured only one defrag runs at a time.
- Rebalanced write-heavy workloads away from control-plane volumes where possible (migrated ephemeral logging writes).

Permanent actions & recommendations:
1) Backup orchestration changes (SRE-8421):
   - Only run snapshot+defrag on one control-plane node at a time (leader-affinity policy: run defrag on non-leader by default).
   - Add pre-check: abort compaction if disk iowait > 10% or etcd p99 > 100ms.
   - Add randomized jitter to scheduled times so jobs do not align across replicas.
2) Instrumentation & detection:
   - New synthetic probe: api->etcd round-trip latency synthetic check (alert at p99 > 250ms).
   - Dashboard tile for defrag/compaction job state with job owner and start/finish times.
3) Runbook additions (see runbook changes section below):
   - Steps to pause backup-runner and drain defrag jobs.
   - Clear guidance for temporarily increasing disk IOPS (cloud console runbook snippet).
4) Capacity & infra changes:
   - Re-evaluate control-plane volume type; consider moving to provisioned IO with higher baseline or larger disk to reduce queue depth sensitivity.
   - Explore snapshot strategy that avoids synchronous defrag on primary disks (e.g., snapshot to separate volume, run defrag against replica copy).

Runbook changes (draft excerpt to append to etcd/control-plane runbook):
- Detection:
  - Monitor etcd p99 and disk iowait. If etcd p99 > 250ms or disk iowait > 20% for 3m, escalate immediately.
- Immediate response:
  1. Pause backup-runner: kubectl -n infra patch cronjob backup-runner -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
  2. Verify defrag processes: ps aux | grep etcd | grep defrag; kill gracefully only if safe and snapshot is complete.
  3. If disk I/O cannot be reduced quickly, open cloud provider change to increase IOPS or attach temporary scratch volume and migrate WAL to it (step-by-step included in runbook appendix).
  4. If leadership is unstable (more than 2 elections in 2m): consider leader-isolation: isolate node with most recent term and follow guidances in etcd operator docs.
- Post-incident:
  - Re-enable the cronjob only after verifying job-run scheduling has been updated to run sequentially and instrumentation checks are in place.

Open questions & items to validate in follow-up testing: 
- Does defrag/compact always need to run on the primary data dir, or can we snapshot+defrag against a copy? (RI-ops explore copy-based defrag)
- Can we change backup-runner to a leader-preferred cron so only one node starts heavy maintenance by default?
- Validate behaviour under high write load: run a chaos test where we generate sustained write churn and then kick off defrag to ensure latency thresholds and guardrails behave as expected.

Follow-ups (owners & rough ETA):
- SRE-8421 (backup-runner orchestration changes) — owner: Priya Patel — ETA: 2025-11-14
- Infra-PR-1123 (increase default control-plane volume IOPS and add automation) — owner: Diego Rios — ETA: 2025-12-01
- Runbook update (etcd-runbook.md) — owner: Maya Chen — ETA: 2025-11-05
- Chaos test (etcd-defrag-load-test) — owner: Liam O'Connor — ETA: 2025-11-20

Appendix (notes for engineers):
- Example etcdctl maintenance defrag command (do NOT run during heavy writes):
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/client.crt --key=/etc/etcd/client.key endpoint defrag
- Quick healthcheck script (local):
  #!/bin/bash
  set -e
  for e in $(echo "https://10.0.0.1:2379 https://10.0.0.2:2379 https://10.0.0.3:2379"); do
    echo "Checking $e"
    curl -sfSk $e/health || echo "unhealthy: $e";
  done

Notes to self: keep this draft lightweight and focused on operational guidance; feed final post-incident writeup to the October incident review and link to SRE oncall playbook.

Document history:
